cards.title: Client
cards.body: ABC Commercial Complex Pvt Ltd, Hinjewadi, Pune.

cards.title: Project Background
cards.body: The client is installing a passenger elevator and requires an independent academic engineering review of selected suspension cables before procurement.

cards.title: Engineering Context
cards.body: You are a mechanical design engineer evaluating whether the suspension cable choice and load distribution appear technically reasonable.

cards.title: Objectives
items: Connect cable safety to Design of Machine Elements.

cards.title: Safety Considerations
cards.body: Elevator suspension cables are safety-critical. Real procurement must comply with applicable codes, certified factor-of-safety requirements, manufacturer data, and professional inspection.

cards.title: Acceptance Criteria
cards.body: Continue only after you understand the client problem, safety context, deliverables, and professional responsibility.

project-charter.acceptanceText: I have read and accepted the EC-01 Project Charter.

identify-components.title: Identify the Components of a Traction Elevator System
identify-components.image: /DesignEngineeringStudio/Engineering Assets Library/EA-01 Traction Elevator System/Student Version/EA-01_Student_v1.0.png
identify-components.description: Student version of the traction elevator system engineering asset with numbered callouts 1-20.

labels.feedback: The electric motor provides rotational input for the traction drive.
The drive sheave transmits traction to the suspension ropes.
The suspension wire ropes carry the elevator car and counterweight.
The elevator car carries passengers between floor levels.
The car frame supports and guides the elevator car assembly.
The counterweight balances part of the car load.
Car guide rails constrain elevator car motion.
Counterweight guide rails constrain counterweight motion.
The deflector sheave guides the rope path.
The machine beam supports machinery loads.
The shaft is the vertical space in which the elevator system operates.
The pit is the lower space beneath the lowest landing.
The pit buffer absorbs impact at the bottom limit of travel.
Top clearance is the space above the car at upper travel.
Landing doors separate each floor from the elevator shaft.
Floor levels indicate the building landings served by the elevator.
The passenger represents the live load carried by the elevator car.
The rope path shows how the suspension ropes are routed.
The elevator motion arrow indicates car travel direction.
The rope movement arrow indicates rope travel over the sheaves.

working-principle.title: Working Principle of Traction Elevator
working-principle.prompt: Explain how a traction elevator works. Include the role of the motor, traction sheave, ropes, counterweight, guide rails, elevator car, controller, and safety gear.

mcq.question: Which component directly provides traction to move the suspension ropes?

material-selection.title: Material Selection
material-selection.prompt: Compare the given candidate materials and recommend the most suitable suspension cable material for this application.

options.title: Mild Steel
options.note: Economical and easy to process but not preferred for high-strength suspension cables.

options.title: High Carbon Steel
options.note: High tensile strength and commonly used in steel wire rope applications.

options.title: Stainless Steel
options.note: Corrosion resistant but grade, cost, and strength must be verified.

options.title: Synthetic Rope
options.note: Lightweight and specialized; requires compatibility, certification, and long-term performance review.

engineering-calculations.title: Engineering Calculations
engineering-calculations.expectedProcess: Passenger load = 750 kg; total static load = 1450 kg; static load per rope = 362.5 kg before applying factor of safety and dynamic effects.

engineering-decision.title: Engineering Decision
engineering-decision.prompt: Decide whether the procurement proposal should be approved, rejected, or redesigned. Provide engineering justification based on safety, material suitability, load distribution, and documentation requirements.
